subject: Discovery recap: FinexCo inference cost squeeze and next steps
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@finexco.com>, Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@finexco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 03 Aug 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: FinExCo inference cost squeeze and next steps

Lena / Miguel — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap so we have alignment and clear next steps.

High-level pain: FinexCo is seeing rapidly rising inference spend tied to a high volume of short, conversational completions (median input ~30 tokens, response ~80 tokens) across two product flows: real-time chat and nightly batch scoring. Current stack: hosted endpoints on a single cloud provider using a mix of gpt-style 7B and a custom 13B variant. Main constraint is unit economics — average cost per completion is above the $0.015 target and procurement is pushing to a <$0.01 goal for the next quarter.

Key call notes (as discussed):
- Workloads: chat (low-latency, p50 ~120ms p95 ~420ms) + batch scoring (non-latency sensitive, throughput peaks overnight).
- Current concurrency: chat ~350 TPS at peak, scoring jobs push ~10k concurrent tokens/hour overnight.
- Priority optimization levers FinexCo is open to: batching/caching, model quantization (they said "open to 4-bit if quality holds"), and fallbacks to smaller model variants for lower-value queries.
- Hard constraints: daytime latency SLOs and strict data residency for EU customers (separate region we'll treat later).

Success criteria you mentioned: reduce per-completion cost to <$0.01 while keeping chat p95 <500ms and maintaining top-line quality (no more than 2-3% regression on intent-classification accuracy).

Immediate asks from Redwood to help scope a pilot:
1) Share 7-day aggregated usage: qps by route, median/95th seq lengths, and percent of requests that are cached-eligible (we provided a short template attached).
2) Confirm whether batch scoring can accept model-variant fallback or must use exact model weights for parity.
3) Approve a short pilot window (2–3 weeks) for us to run: a mixed strategy combining prefix caching for repeated prompts, dynamic batching for chat, and a quantized 4-bit variant for scoring jobs.

Attachments: finexco-inference-cost-worksheet.xlsx (usage template), redwood-qtrly-pricing-guidelines.pdf (pricing/discount band reference).

Proposed next steps:
- You (Lena) populate and return the worksheet by EOD Thu 8/6.
- Karthik will scope the expected cost savings range and required infra changes after we review the worksheet.
- Dev will propose a technical plan for integrating caching and batching into your chat route (2–3 engineering days to wire prototype).

If that aligns, I’ll schedule a 30-min technical sync for early next week. Thanks again — I’ll follow up with calendar options.

—
Soojín Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0191

From: Lena Park <lena.park@finexco.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Miguel Torres <miguel.torres@finexco.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: FinExCo inference cost squeeze and next steps

Thanks Soojin — clear and helpful. A few clarifications from our side:

- The numbers you called out are in the right ballpark. Our p95 for chat is closer to 480ms on the fastest region but spikes up to 650ms for cross-region fallbacks.
- For batch scoring, model parity is preferred, but we can accept a quantized variant if we can re-run a held-out validation set to confirm <1.5% accuracy drift.
- We estimate ~40% of chat interactions are repeats (good candidates for prefix caching) and ~25% of scoring inputs are identical across nightly runs.

We’ll fill the attached worksheet. Quick ask for Redwood: can you include an example of how you estimate cache hit rate improvements? That will help our procurement team model the economics.

I’ll aim to return the worksheet by Thu 8/6 EOD. Also ok to lock a 30-min technical sync next Tue (8/11).

Best,
Lena Park
Head of AI Ops | FinexCo
lena.park@finexco.com | +1 (212) 555-4433

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@finexco.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: FinExCo inference cost squeeze and next steps

Lena — quick technical notes to set expectations before the tech sync: 

1) Batching: For low-latency chat, we typically run a small dynamic batch window (~5–15ms) which keeps p50/p95 impact minimal while improving throughput. We'll prototype conservative batch windows first and measure end-to-end latency.

2) Caching: Prefix caching yields the best wins on high-repeat flows. Our bench has shown 30–50% token savings on repeat-heavy chat datasets. We’ll provide a per-route model of expected hit rates once we see the worksheet.

3) Quantization: 4-bit quantization for your 13B variant is plausible; quality varies by model family and tokenizer. We’ll include a validation run as part of the pilot and provide a rollback path to 8-bit if needed.

If you can include a small sample of 10k anonymized prompts (or hashed variants) we can run a dry simulation to estimate cache hits and batching benefits without you sharing raw PII.

—Karthik
Director, Model Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Lena Park <lena.park@finexco.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: FinExCo inference cost squeeze and next steps

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Lena — that timeline works. Summary of agreed next steps and owners: 

- FinexCo: complete the attached worksheet + optionally upload 10k hashed prompts to the secure share (due Thu 8/6 EOD) — Lena.
- Redwood (Karthik): run dry simulations on hashed sample, return estimated cache hit rates and projected unit cost range (2 business days after receiving data).
- Redwood (Dev): draft a 2–3 day integration plan for batching + prefix cache in your chat route and a separate plan for overnight scoring fallback to quantized variant.
- Commercial: I’ll produce a short pilot SOW and a provisional pricing band once we have the worksheet (targeting a 3-week pilot).

I’ll send calendar invites for the tech sync (Tue 8/11) and the commercial kickoff after we get the worksheet. If anything changes on timing, flag me directly.

Thanks — looking forward.

—
Soojín
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
